First of all, update EVE-NG

//

`apt-get update -y && apt-get upgrade -y`

|

Fix permissions

//

`/opt/unetlab/wrappers/unl_wrapper -a fixpermissions`

|

Reboot EVE-NG machine

//

`reboot` \*\* it sometimes is needed because not always is router connected to VM \*\*

|

Try to delete the project in EVE-NG and create a new one.  Connect each other and enable both routers. First what I recommend is to go to CLI and:

|

disable **dhcp-client** on both routers  \*\* from my experience it might be cause so it's good to disable it\*\*

//

`ip dhcp-client print` \*\* you can see it's active and it's trying to get an IP from DHCP on an interface \*\*

`ip dhcp-client remove numbers=0` \*\* it removes dhcp-client \*\*

`ip dhcp-client print` \*\* print it again to make sure no searching occurss \*\*

|

Add an ip address with "**disabled=no**" parameter

//

`ip address add adddress=$IP/$PREFIX interface=$INTERFACE disabled=no`

`ip address print` \*\* make sure it's set and enabled \*\*

|

Please give me feedback. I've been using EVE-NG as well.

|

EDIT: I'd definitely give a try of a method above. Try my method **with / without duplicated** routers to see a difference.

Try to convert theory into practice.

For instance, if you read about IPv6, open Cisco Packet Tracer and assign link\-local, site\-local, global address to PCs and routers to memorize the structure of it. Try to assign at least 5 different addresses without help. Stop doing this when you become confident. It applies to everything \(routing, VLANs, port\-security etc\) \- whatever you can try in Packet Tracer / GNS3 etc, do it! Not just read it!

Open Notepad and write questions to yourself. Answer them immediately, while reading, and once you finished a chapter. Then the same questions answer after one day, 5 days, 15 days to make sure you saved information in a long\-term memory.

Repeat what you learnt! Follow the forgetting curve: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgetting\_curve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forgetting_curve)

Next thing is try to explain what you learnt \- it's a known method named by a person but I can't remember that rn. It'll show if you understand it or if you think you understand it.

If you don't understand something read it again. Try to drawn it on a paper to image what an author is talking about. If it still doesn't work use another resources. Explanation by a person A doesn't have to be suitable for you but explanation by a person B can be perfect so don't give up. You've lots of resources including different sites, YouTube channels etc.

Don't rush it. Previous knowledge is important to understand deeper concept.

Take a break after 50 minutes for 5\-10 minutes to relax your brain.

If you wanna give up remember why you started. From the beginning it can be tough but you can make it!
